articles.title: I fed a global bird model foreign audio. It was confidently wrong. Then I fixed it.
articles.excerpt: Opening I started this project because I noticed something wrong with how bird identification works in my own town. BirdNET is a genuinely impressive open-source project. Point it at a recording and i…
articles.body: Opening I started this project because I noticed something wrong with how bird identification works in my own town. BirdNET is a genuinely impressive open-source project. Point it at a recording and it will confidently tell you what you heard. I tried it on some audio recorded on my hostel campus in Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu, and it told me about Rose-ringed Parakeet, Common Grackle, and Dark-eyed Junco . The grackle is a North American species. It has never been in India. It was never in my garden. The model was not confused — it was sure , and wrong. That is the whole problem in one clip. A global classifier trained on global audio will happily tell you about birds that live four thousand kilometres away, because nothing in its architecture knows or cares where you are standing.

articles.title: Your related items panel can name records the viewer can't open
articles.excerpt: Related / "People also viewed" panels usually query by shared tag, same parent, or embedding neighbor. That query is scoped by workspace_id and maybe deleted_at IS NULL. It rarely re-runs the viewer's…
articles.body: Related / "People also viewed" panels usually query by shared tag, same parent, or embedding neighbor. That query is scoped by workspace_id and maybe deleted_at IS NULL . It rarely re-runs the viewer's read check on each neighbor. A contractor opens a deal they can see. The sidebar lists "Acme renewal (legal hold)" because that record shares a tag. The contractor cannot open Acme. The title already leaked. When you build the related list for a viewer, run the same read check the detail page uses on every candidate. Drop rows that fail. Don't show a locked icon next to a title the viewer was not allowed to know. Quick test: as a limited viewer, open a public record that shares a tag with a private one. If the private title shows in Related, the panel skipped the check.

articles.body: Some agent tasks have a small, structured output: choose a department, estimate whether an incident needs escalation, or place a message on an urgency rubric. OpenClaw's developers added native support for a separate Decision model role. Our plugin connects local Tev1 models running in Ollama to that existing infrastructure. We built Ollama Decision , an independent MIT-licensed community plugin supporting Tev1 0.8B and 4B through Ollama's System One API. The agent keeps its conversational model; a Decision call evaluates the supplied state against explicit questions. A concrete example Use this synthetic state: Checkout is failing for all customers. Ask three independent questions: Boolean: Does this require incident response? Choice: Is Support or Billing responsible?

articles.title: Lifeform 🌿 — Turning Outdoor Exploration Into a Nature Discovery Game

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass . 🌿 Lifeform — Explore. Discover. Build. What I Built Lifeform is a nature-exploration game that encourages people to step outside, discover living things, and build a digital collection of their discoveries. The idea is simple: instead of spending more time scrolling, go outside and notice the living world around you. With Lifeform, you can photograph a plant, bird, insect, fungus, or other animal and ask an AI naturalist to identify it. Here's how the experience works: Explore: Head outdoors and find something interesting. Discover: Upload a photo and receive an AI-generated identification, confidence level, and description. Collect: Add new discoveries to your collection.

On Friday, the agency released its final Request for Proposals inviting industry to submit plans for the next generation of commercial space stations. “In alignment with the President’s National Space Policy, NASA is committed to maintaining a sustained American presence in low Earth orbit long after the International Space Station retires,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “We will continue to need a place to conduct research, develop technologies, train crews, and prepare for missions to the Moon and Mars.

articles.title: NASA Demonstrates Next-Generation Heat Shield Technologies
articles.excerpt: NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24th cargo resupply missi…
articles.body: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) A KREPE-3 capsule floats inside the Northrup Grumman Cygnus XL 24 cargo spacecraft on October 7. Inside the capsule is a 3-D printed heat shield designed by researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. NASA NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24 th cargo resupply mission for NASA undocked from the International Space Station, it carried a fleet of 12 small, experimental capsules designed to test the next generation of thermal protection materials that could serve as the foundation for future heat shields.
